title: Server‑Side Rendering with getServerSideProps
description: Generate fresh HTML on every request. Perfect for personalised dashboards and real‑time data.

slides.title: Always Fresh Data 🍃
Dashboard with SSR (pages/dashboard.js)
slides.content: Fetch user‑specific data on every request. The `context` object contains `req`, `res`, `params`, `query`.

quizData.question: What does `getServerSideProps` receive that `getStaticProps` does not?

options.text: Access to the request object (req, res)

quizData.explanation: `getServerSideProps` runs per request, so it receives the HTTP request and response objects, allowing you to read headers, cookies, etc.

slides.title: Performance Considerations ⚖️
slides.content:
# SSR vs SSG Speed

* **SSG**: Pages served from CDN, extremely fast TTFB. Best for public content.
* **SSR**: Server must compute on every request. Higher TTFB. Can be mitigated with caching (CDN, `Cache-Control` headers).

Next.js also supports **ISR** (Incremental Static Regeneration) as a middle ground – we’ll cover that soon.

Use SSR only when you truly need real‑time or user‑specific data on the initial HTML.

slides.title: Return Redirect from getServerSideProps (pages/old-page.js)
slides.content: You can also return `redirect` or `notFound` just like in `getStaticProps`.

quizData.question: Which of these is the best use case for `getServerSideProps`?

options.text: A marketing landing page that rarely changes
A real‑time stock ticker dashboard that must show user‑specific data

quizData.explanation: SSR is ideal for pages that change frequently or depend on the user making the request, like dashboards.
